A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepDistributedQP research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–I. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of equations, figures, tables and appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments, including optimality-gap curves, runtime comparisons, policy comparisons and evaluated generalization bounds in Section 6 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including Figures 5–7 and the detailed runtime and iteration results in Appendix I, Table 6.

M1.justification: DistributedQP updates, DeepDistributedQP and DeepQP architectures, feedback policies, training loss and solution procedures are unchanged in Sections 3–4 and their supporting appendices.

E1.justification: Both retain the same random QP, centralized and multi-agent control, portfolio optimization, network flow and LASSO tasks. The citation-label changes in Appendix I do not alter benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same OSQP and DistributedQP comparator variants, including fixed/adaptive penalties and direct/indirect OSQP timing comparisons. The newly cited learning-to-optimize primer is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Iteration budgets, optimality-gap metrics, problem dimensions, training/testing sample counts, initialization and optimizer settings remain unchanged in Section 6 and Appendix I, including Tables 1–5.

E4.justification: The open-loop versus closed-loop and local versus shared policy comparisons, scalability analyses and empirical generalization-bound evaluation are retained unchanged in Figures 5–7 and Section 6.2.

E5.justification: Statistical estimation and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, including the 30,000 sampled weights and 99% probability guarantee used for empirical PAC-Bayes bound evaluation. No repeated-run or seed reporting is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 5–7 and Table 6 retain the same curves, numerical results, runtime comparisons and generalization-bound findings. No result entries, rankings or qualitative experimental findings are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Formal definitions, Assumption 1, Theorems 1–3, convergence proofs, implicit-differentiation derivation and PAC-Bayes mathematics are unchanged, including the supporting appendices. The changed appendix citations leave equations intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same novelty, convergence, generalization, scalability and efficiency claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of policy benefits and scalability, direct-versus-indirect solver tradeoffs, and limitations concerning pre-solved training data and average-performance guarantees remain unchanged in Section 6 and Appendix I.

D1.justification: Hardware, data-generation instructions, network and training hyperparameters, optimizer configuration and training-time disclosures are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds T. Chen et al., Learning to optimize: A primer and a benchmark (2022b), and cites it in the introductory learning-to-optimize discussion. The existing S. W. Chen et al. control paper becomes 2022a and remains the Appendix I benchmark source. Broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an ICLR 2025 acceptance/preprint notice and updates the arXiv version/date and Chen citation labels. The prose and section/appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first page gains an acceptance header and a slight text-position adjustment. The added reference changes bibliography spacing and page breaks; all seven figures and six tables retain their presentation and placement.

improvement.justification: The introduction now identifies the learning-to-optimize primer, while the control benchmark citations are explicitly distinguished as the existing MPC paper. This modestly improves attribution and reference traceability. The scientific arguments, experimental evidence and limitations are unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
